about.heading: What is Meichu Hackathon?
about.body: Meichu Hackathon is a two-day, one-night cross-disciplinary implementation competition. Student teams turn abstract ideas into minimum viable products (MVPs) within limited time. The competition has two tracks:

tracks.title: Hacker Track
tracks.body: The Hacker Track is built around challenges from corporate partners, who provide dedicated resources such as APIs or hardware. Participants need programming skills and solve corporate problems through technical implementation.

tracks.title: Maker Exchange Track
tracks.body: The Maker Exchange Track is proposed by the Hsinchu City Government. It does not require programming background and encourages students from different departments to use their expertise together to propose diverse solutions for social issues.

eventInfo.heading: 2026 Basic Event Info
eventInfo.note: This block is designed as a card layout so yearly data can be quickly replaced.

cards.label: Eligible participants
cards.value: Students from colleges and universities across Taiwan. The Maker Exchange Track also opens to high school students.

cards.label: Registration fee
cards.value: NT$1,000 per person, plus a NT$100 deposit

cards.label: Special discount
cards.value: To encourage cross-disciplinary teams, teams with three or more different departments receive NT$100 off per person.

cards.label: Low-income support
cards.value: Registration is free for low- and middle-low-income participants.

items.title: Direct company access
items.body: Pre-event exclusive workshops and company visits, plus on-site technical staff during the competition, help you access the latest industry resources directly.

items.title: Prize money beyond ten thousand
items.body: Hacker Track: first place selected by each company can receive NT$25,000 and internship or interview opportunities, with a further chance to compete for the Meichu Grand Prize of up to NT$30,000.

items.title: Maker Exchange awards
items.body: Maker Exchange Track: the top prize reaches NT$50,000, with multiple creative awards as well.

items.title: A packed extreme challenge
items.body: During the two-day, one-night implementation period, dinner, midnight snacks, and rich on-site entertainment are provided.

stats.title: A benchmark scale
stats.body: In 2025, total participants reached 242, and total venue foot traffic reached 4,283 visits.

stats.title: Cross-disciplinary is the point
stats.body: Although about 60% of participants came from electrical engineering, computer science, and engineering colleges, management, design, biomedical, and other fields also had strong representation. The Maker Exchange Track attracted nearly half of its participants from diverse departments.

stats.title: Top campuses gathered
stats.body: The event brings together elite students from National Tsing Hua University, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, National Taiwan University, National Cheng Kung University, National Taiwan Normal University, National Central University, and other top universities across Taiwan.

slices.label: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

items.q: Q: Can I participate if I cannot code?
items.a: A: Absolutely. We have the Maker Exchange Track and strongly encourage cross-disciplinary teams. A strong project also needs planning, design, and business analysis talent.

items.q: Q: Is the schedule only two short days?
items.a: A: Not only that. Before the official competition, we plan company visits and workshops for getting familiar with company resources, so you can receive technical guidance before the event.

items.q: Q: Who owns the intellectual property of the work?
items.a: A: The ownership of the code and project belongs entirely to the participants. Corporate partners and organizers only hold the right to publicly display the works and creative ideas.

items.q: Q: What if I do not have teammates?
items.a: A: We have a Facebook group to help match participants. Search for "Match at MCH" and join the group to find the best teammates for you.
